sections.h2: Who handles a Gallatin County tax bill
sections.html:
Three Warsaw offices come into play when a house changes hands. The PVA places the value, the Sheriff's Office collects payment, and the County Clerk records deeds and accepts assessment appeals.

  • PVA: 200 Washington Street (mail to PO Box 470), Warsaw, KY 41095, phone (859) 567-5621.
  • Sheriff: 106 North Main (mail to PO Box 1025), Warsaw, phone (859) 567-5751. The county's sheriff page links to a tax bill lookup.
  • County Clerk: 803 East Main Street, Warsaw, phone (859) 567-5411, weekdays to 4:30 p.m.

The City of Warsaw runs its own online payment page for water, sewer and property tax bills, which means a house within city limits can owe two governments. Before you pick a closing date, ask the sheriff and the city what is attached to the address, and hold on to every paid receipt for the buyer's title company. A clean paper trail shortens the closing, because the title search will list any unpaid balance as an exception.

sections.h2: Gallatin County housing and the local market
sections.html:
At about 105 square miles, Gallatin ranks near the bottom of the state by size, on the Ohio River across from Indiana and part of the Cincinnati metropolitan area. Warsaw is the seat, with Sparta and Glencoe the other communities. Interstate 71 runs through with three exits around Sparta and Glencoe, joined by US 42 and US 127, and the commute averages 29.5 minutes. A good share of residents work elsewhere in the region.

The 2020 census found 3,685 housing units with 13.1 percent unoccupied, so a share of the stock is seasonal, vacant or waiting for a buyer. Growth has been slow but steady, and the 2020 count classed all residents as rural, so many sellers own acreage or a riverside lot rather than a city parcel. Have your parcel number and the property address ready when you call any of the three offices, so staff can pull the right record without a second call.

Payment goes to the sheriff, and KRS 134.015 sets one schedule for every owner. A bill paid whole by November 1 drops 2 percent. Between then and December 31 you owe the printed figure. Each late month costs more: 5 percent in January, 10 percent past that.

If bill mailing slips, the Department of Revenue can replace the usual dates with a compressed schedule of one month at a discount, one month at face and one month at 5 percent, so go by the dates printed on your own bill. After a sale, give the sheriff the buyer's name so future bills land with the right person.

You can pay at the sheriff's office on North Main, mail a payment to PO Box 1025, or look up the bill on the sheriff page first to confirm the amount. With a mortgage escrow, check that the servicer actually got the bill, because it cannot pay what it never received. Anything unpaid after the late dates is turned over in April, so do not leave a sale-year bill for the buyer to find.

Begin at the PVA office, 200 Washington Street. A PVA conference must come before an appeal, and it is easiest to go right after assessment notices arrive. The tax roll then opens to public view for 13 days in early May.

Once you have talked with the PVA or a deputy, put the appeal in writing and give it to the County Clerk's office by the end of the first business day after public viewing closes. A local review board then convenes roughly four to five weeks on and can sit up to five days.

  • Bring details on the land and buildings, construction costs, insurance records and listings of similar properties.
  • Expect to explain your evidence in person with the PVA also present.
  • The board must put the reason for any raise or cut in writing, and you are allowed to record the hearing.

Skipping a hearing you filed for shuts off the next step, the Kentucky Claims Commission, so write the hearing date down the day you learn it.

For seniors and totally disabled owners, $49,100 is deducted from assessed value in 2025 and 2026. File with the Gallatin County PVA. Because the typical home here is valued at $178,200, the deduction takes a meaningful bite out of the taxable amount.

Disability filers must document payments from a federal agency or a retirement system that cover the whole assessment period, and they renew each year. The yearly renewal is waived for owners with a service-connected military disability and for anyone Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled totally and permanently disabled.

If you sell, tell the PVA so the exemption is removed from your name. The buyer can apply for their own if they qualify, and the form has to be filed with the Gallatin County PVA office in Warsaw rather than with the sheriff or the clerk.

Unpaid tax does not disappear at closing. The owner personally owes the tax from the assessment date under KRS 134.015, and a lien for delinquency under KRS 134.420 rides along with the parcel whoever takes title.

Every open bill is handed from the sheriff to the County Clerk on April 15 as a certificate of delinquency. The county attorney then sends a first notice inside 30 days and a second inside 60. A clerk's sale can follow 90 to 135 days after the handover. A third-party buyer at that sale can pile on substantial fees.

  1. Phone the sheriff, (859) 567-5751, for a payoff before listing.
  2. If the house is in Warsaw, ask the city whether a water, sewer or city tax bill is open too.
  3. Give the title company that number and it will pay the balance from your proceeds.
  4. Keep the paid receipts. The title search lists any unpaid balance as an exception to clean title.

Cash buyers who take a house as-is do not wait on a lender, and the tax is settled at the table. That suits an owner facing repairs and back taxes together. With no appraisal step, timing rests on the title work and the payoff letter.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Gallatin County property tax payment?
faqs.a: Mail or bring it to the Gallatin County Sheriff, 106 North Main in Warsaw, or PO Box 1025, Warsaw, KY 41095. The county's sheriff page links a tax bill lookup.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Gallatin County PVA?
faqs.a: Call (859) 567-5621 or visit 200 Washington Street in Warsaw. The PVA handles value questions, exemption forms and owner records.

faqs.q: When is the early-payment date in Gallatin County?
faqs.a: The date is the same statewide: November 1. A full payment by then saves 2 percent, and the printed amount is owed until December 31.

faqs.q: Does the City of Warsaw send its own tax bill?
faqs.a: Warsaw offers an online page for water, sewer and property tax bills. If the house is inside the city, check with both the city and the sheriff about which bills apply.

faqs.q: Does a tax lien survive a sale in Gallatin County?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien stays with the property after a sale until the tax is paid or the KRS 134.420 period runs out, so clear the balance at closing.
